name: Martin Takes Daily Vitamins
description: Martin sits on a futon couch, watching MTV with the sound off. In front of him, a row of vitamin bottles lines the coffee table. He picks up several capsules from each bottle, swallows them one by one, and washes them down with a reddish-orange beverage.
related_events: Martin takes daily vitamin supplements with a reddish-orange drink

name: Martin Drives Toward His Past
description: Martin drives down a long roadway, the landscape shifting subtly as he moves deeper into familiar territory. The road stretches ahead, lined with markers that hint at memories long buried. He passes an old gas station, its sign rusted but still legible, then a faded billboard he once knew by heart. The car hums steadily, carrying him closer to a town he hasn't seen in years, where the streets and buildings remain unchanged, waiting.
related_events: Martin drives down the roadway toward his past

name: Martin Enters the Bedroom Silently
description: Martin crouches low and moves quietly down the hallway. He reaches the bedroom, pauses briefly at the doorway, and then slips across the threshold without making a sound. A woman's voice speaks from somewhere nearby: 'Whenever news of you filters back, the school is excited and proud of your accomplishments...'
related_events: Martin stealthily enters the bedroom

name: Martin Returns to the Station
description: Martin stops moving forward, his expression shifting briefly before he turns around and walks back toward the station.
related_events: Martin changes his mind and returns to the station

name: Martin Reads Kill Without Joy and Then Iron John on a Red-Eye Flight
description: Martin sits in a first-class seat on a red-eye flight to the Midwest. He has finished reading a magazine and places it on the empty seat beside him. He sets a Powerbar aside and opens the book Kill Without Joy, reading for a time. After a moment, he closes the book and puts it down. He then picks up another book, Iron John, and begins reading it.
related_events: Martin reads Kill Without Joy on a red-eye flight
Martin switches from reading Kill Without Joy to reading Iron John

name: Martin Exits Station with Strained Expression
description: Martin steps out of the storefront station in the Grosse Pointe shopping district and comes to an abrupt stop in the middle of the street. His face shows a look of strain.
related_events: Martin exits storefront station with strained expression

name: Martin Hides the Briefcase Behind the Wall Vent
description: Martin enters the room, walks to the bed, and kicks a leather bag underneath it. He picks up a steel-sided briefcase, crouches near the wall, and pries off a vent cover. He slides the briefcase into the opening behind the wall, then fits the vent cover back into place.
related_events: Martin enters the room and hides a briefcase behind a wall vent

name: Grocer Makes and Takes Vegetable Juice
description: Track light fills the gourmet-rustic kitchen. Grocer, wearing a burgundy Fila sweat suit, pushes beets into a vegetable juicer. Piles of celery and carrots sit beside the machine. The juicer hums as it processes the vegetables. Grocer fills a glass with the resulting juice, lifts it from the machine, and carries it out of the kitchen.
related_events: Grocer prepares vegetable juice in the kitchen
Grocer exits the kitchen with a glass of juice

name: Martin Arrives at the Apartment
description: Martin walks into a sparsely furnished apartment. He carries a carry-on bag and a briefcase, which he lets fall in the hallway.
related_events: Martin enters sparsely furnished apartment
Martin drops carry-on bag and briefcase in hallway

name: Martin Flips Through Magazines on a First-Class Flight
description: Martin sits in a first-class seat with the tray table down. A stack of magazines rests on the left side of the tray—Sports Illustrated, Mademoiselle, Wired, Rolling Stone, National Review, Spin, National Geographic, and others. He takes one from the top, flips through it quickly, glancing at images: a toothless hockey player raising a stick in triumph, a lineup of Sony products, a crouched child in a famine-stricken area with a vulture in the distance, a supermodel in suede, a pack of Tic Tacs, former U.S. Presidents walking arm in arm, smiling. He reads nothing, moves on after a few seconds, and places the magazine into the empty seat beside him. He draws the next one and repeats the process.
related_events: Martin flips through magazines on a first class flight

name: Lardner and McCullers Watch Martin in the Street
description: Lardner and McCullers stand together, their eyes fixed on Martin, who is motionless in the middle of the street. They exchange a glance, their brows furrowed, and remain still, watching him closely.
related_events: Lardner and McCullers observe Martin standing in the street
Lardner and McCullers frown while contemplating Martin's next move

name: Debi Begins Broadcast About Mysterious Visitor
description: Debi sits upright, reaches for the console, and flips the ON-AIR switch. She speaks into the microphone: 'A man comes to you. He is from the past, bringing pain long since put behind you. He says peculiar things and leaves abruptly. It all comes flooding back.'
related_events: Debi flips the ON-AIR switch and begins a radio broadcast
Debi narrates a mysterious visitor from the past

name: Martin Visits His Father's Grave
description: Martin pulls the car to a stop at the cemetery and looks out the window at the rows of headstones. He raises his hand in a stiff wave. 'Hey Pop... You got off easy. The house is a 7-11. Mom's a psycho-pharmacological punching bag and I murder for cash. If you were here I think you'd be proud.' He puts the car in gear and drives away.
related_events: Martin stops the car at the cemetery
Martin delivers a sarcastic farewell to his deceased father
Martin drives away from the cemetery

name: Martin and the Driver Talk of Solitude
description: After arriving at Kennedy Airport, Martin settles into the back seat of the livery as it weaves through the arrival lanes. The driver asks how his day was. Martin says it was effective, but admits he has lost his passion for work. The driver asks if he likes the people he works with. Martin replies that he works alone. The driver nods, saying that explains it. He says he’s always been alone and that’s why he’s a good driver. He describes how he can think on his feet, survive, and stay calm even when waiting for hours in front of a house. He contrasts himself with other drivers who grow angry and impatient, shouting for passengers to hurry. He points out that no matter what, they all end up back in the garage by evening. He asks what the big deal is, saying you leave in the morning and return at night—it’s all the same.
related_events: Martin begins conversation with driver after arriving at Kennedy Airport
Driver reflects on solitude as a professional strength
Driver explains tolerance for long waits without frustration

name: Martin Finds a 7-11 Where His House Once Stood
description: Martin stands in front of a 7-11, staring at the building as if he is looking at a landscape from another world. He takes out his phone and dials a number. MARTIN (into phone) Dr. Oatman. Dr. Oatman. Please pick up if you're there... It's Martin Blank. It's gone. My house. It's not here. My house is gone and now there's a 7-11 here... And that's unfortunate... You can never go home again, Dr. Oatman. He ends the call and watches people walking in and out of the store, buying drinks and snacks. MARTIN (to himself) But I guess you can shop there.
related_events: Martin discovers his house has been replaced by a 7-11
Martin calls Dr. Oatman to report his house is gone
Martin reflects on the impossibility of returning home

name: Martin Cleans and Reads During Final Approach
description: Martin sits in his first-class seat and unfolds an airline hot towel, wiping his face and hands. He folds the towel neatly and picks up a stack of magazines, flipping quickly through the pages. As he sets them aside, the pilot's voice comes over the intercom, announcing that the weather in Chicago is seventy-six degrees and partly cloudy.
related_events: Martin uses airline hot towel to wipe face and hands
Martin flips through stack of magazines
Pilot makes announcement about Chicago weather

name: Debi Confronts Martin's Return
description: Debi stands in the broadcast booth, her breath catching as Martin walks into the police station. He moves toward her, crossing the threshold of the booth without a word. The air shifts. They face each other, silent, the space between them charged. No one speaks, but the tension rises, thick and palpable, as the past settles into the room.
related_events: Debi experiences emotional shock upon seeing Martin
Martin walks back into the police station
Martin enters the broadcast booth
Tension escalates between Debi and Martin

name: End of the Therapy Session
description: The therapy session nears its end. Dr. Oatman shows visible relief that the time is almost up. Martin sits back, dismissing the idea of morality as unimportant. When Dr. Oatman suggests he attend his upcoming reunion to reconnect with people from his past, Martin responds with a deadpan remark: if he gets restless, he might kill a few small animals. Dr. Oatman pauses, then says, 'Now we're making progress,' as the session concludes.
related_events: Dr. Oatman expresses relief that therapy session is ending
Martin dismisses morality as irrelevant
Martin threatens to kill small animals if feeling restless
Dr. Oatman suggests Martin attend his reunion

name: Lardner and McCullers Discuss Past Media Manipulations
description: Lardner brings up an incident where Frysal's men paid a Deejay in Cairo to announce a fake press conference. He then mentions the Munich Olympics in 1972, noting that a local radio station began broadcasting news of the massacre two minutes before it actually happened. McCullers responds, attributing the Munich incident to the Bader-Meinhof Group, but Lardner corrects him, stating it was the PLO.
related_events: Frysal's men bribe Deejay in Cairo to announce fake press conference
Munich Olympics massacre broadcast begins prematurely
Lardner corrects McCullers on responsible group for Munich incident

name: Detectives Spot Martin Arriving in Town Car
description: Lardner and McCullers sit in their car along the main strip, keeping watch. Lardner dozes, his face pressed against the passenger window. McCullers leans back, idly tapping a to-go cup in his lap while softly singing. As Martin's Town Car comes down the street, McCullers stops mid-verse, recognizing the vehicle. He turns and nudges Lardner, then points. Martin pulls into a space on the street outside the radio station and gets out, looking nervous.
related_events: McCullers recognizes Martin's Town Car approaching
McCullers nudges Lardner to alert him

name: Martin Arrives at the Radio Station
description: Martin drives his Town Car down the quiet street and pulls into a parking space in front of the radio station. He turns off the engine, opens the door, and steps out, glancing around as he closes the door behind him. His movements are tense, his posture stiff, and he pauses briefly, looking up at the building with a nervous expression before taking a step toward the entrance.
related_events: Martin parks outside the radio station
Martin exits his vehicle looking nervous

name: Martin Finds an Old Photo Album
description: In a dimly lit apartment with black furniture and no decorations, Martin kneels beside a cardboard box and sifts through its contents. He pulls out a photo album and opens it. The first page shows a photograph of himself as a teenager, standing beside his mother, who smiles gently but has tired eyes. Opposite the photo is a gilt-edged funeral announcement for Victor Allen Blank. Martin turns the page and sees a picture of a young girl in a winter coat, Debi Newberry, her hand scrawled message reading, "Would you rather...?!" A cat sits nearby, watching him, and meows.
related_events: Martin sorts through cardboard box and discovers photo album
Martin views teenage photograph of himself and his mother
Martin reads funeral announcement for Victor Allen Blank

name: Martin Finds a Photo of Deb Newberry While the Cat Watches
description: Martin turns the page of the photo album and sees a photograph of Deb Newberry, a tall, thin girl in a bulky winter coat, smiling brightly. The cat meows, watching him as he looks at the image. Handwritten on the photo in looping script is the question: "Would you rather...?"
related_events: Martin turns page of photo album and sees photograph of Deb Newberry
Cat meows while observing Martin
Cat observes Martin while meowing

name: Martin Arrives to Visit Mary
description: The nurse walks down the hallway with Martin, then enters a sunlit room where Mary sits on the edge of the bed, holding her purse and a cigarette. The nurse gently helps Mary to her feet. Mary takes hold of Martin's arm, and they begin to move out of the room together.
related_events: Nurse leads Martin to Mary's room
Nurse assists Mary from the bed

name: Martin and Mary Reunite in the Sunlit Room
description: A nurse leads Martin down a drab, antiseptic hallway and into a sunlit room, where Mary sits on the edge of the bed, clutching her purse and a filterless Pall-Mall, wearing a light coat. The nurse says, "Mary, your son's here," and gently helps her to her feet. Martin hugs her stiffly, patting her shoulders. Mary reaches out and takes hold of his arm. They begin walking out of the room together.
related_events: Martin hugs Mary awkwardly
Mary grasps Martin's arm
Martin and Mary begin leaving the room

name: Martin Gets His Car and Leaves
description: The valet pulls up Martin's rented Town Car and stops near the curb. Martin meets him at the trunk, hands over a tip, and takes the keys. He walks around and gets into the driver's seat. As he does, he pulls a laminated 'Personal Pan Power' card from his pocket, looks at it briefly, and drops it onto the asphalt. The card lies on the ground as a police car approaches, its wheel rolling to a stop directly over the discarded card. Martin starts the engine and drives away.
related_events: Valet delivers Martin's rented Town Car
Martin exchanges tip for car keys with valet
Martin discards 'Personal Pan Power' card onto the ground

name: Martin Drives Away as Police Arrive
description: Martin walks toward his rented Town Car as the valet pulls it up. He meets the valet at the trunk, exchanges a tip for the keys, and reaches inside to retrieve a laminated 'Personal Pan Power' card. He looks at it briefly before tossing it onto the ground. In the distance, police cars appear, winding down the long club driveway. Martin gets into the car, starts the engine, and pulls away. The discarded card lies on the asphalt as a police car rolls forward and stops, its rear wheel coming to rest directly on top of the card.
related_events: Police cars arrive at the club driveway
Martin enters his car and drives away
Police car wheel rolls over discarded laminated card

name: Martin Drives onto Turnpike and Changes Radio Station
description: Martin steers a black Lincoln Town Car off the airport access road and onto a turnpike. The car accelerates past a fixed point on the road, continuing into the distance. Inside, the radio plays a news broadcast about weather and a stock market scandal involving a U.S.-Japanese tech venture. Martin flips through the stations, briefly landing on Rush Limbaugh, muttering 'Mein hero' under his breath. He then switches to a slow reggae track, 'Armageddon Time' by The Clash, which fills the car as he drives on.
related_events: Martin drives black Lincoln Town Car from airport to turnpike
Martin's car passes camera position on the road
Martin changes radio station from Rush Limbaugh to The Clash

name: Lardner and McCullers Follow Martin on the Turnpike
description: A mid-eighties Ford Country Squire station wagon pulls onto the turnpike shortly after Martin's black Lincoln Town Car. Inside the station wagon, Lardner and McCullers sit in silence, listening to the radio. The broadcast reports on stock market fluctuations and a growing scandal at the U.S.-Japanese Tech Center, where safety flaws in next year's vehicle models have been exposed by an unknown whistle-blower. The same news plays in Martin's car as he drives ahead, the sound of Rush Limbaugh briefly cutting through before he changes the station to a slow reggae track. The two vehicles move down the road, one following the other, each tuned to the same broadcast.
related_events: Ford Country Squire station wagon follows Martin's car
Lardner and McCullers listen to news broadcast in station wagon
News broadcast reports on stock fluctuations and Tech Center scandal

name: Martin Feeds the Cat and Takes His Supplement
description: Martin pulls himself away from the album as the cat follows, meowing hungrily. He opens a restaurant-style refrigerator filled with bottles of vitamins, spirulina, wheatgrass, digestible hydrogen peroxide, fluoride treatment, oxygenated mouth rinse, and thirty cans of CATFOOD. He asks the cat, 'Tuna or liver?' The cat meows in response. Martin selects a can of tuna-flavored cat food, opens it, and sets it down for the cat to eat. At the same time, he takes a bottle of his own nutritional supplement from the refrigerator and opens it for himself.
related_events: Martin decides to leave the album and moves toward the refrigerator
Cat requests food while following Martin
Martin selects and opens tuna-flavored cat food
Cat consumes tuna-flavored cat food from the can
Martin retrieves and opens his own nutritional supplement

name: Martin Finds the Yearbook
description: After the cat begins eating, Martin walks back to the cardboard box and pulls out a yearbook. He flips it open and looks at a photo of a group of teenagers dressed in Blues Brothers costumes, posing for the camera. He turns the page and sees a picture of sprinters straining toward a finish line. He continues flipping until he reaches a senior portrait of Debi Newbery. Her name is printed beneath a photo that includes him, their images side by side.
related_events: Martin returns to the cardboard box and discovers a yearbook
Martin flips open the yearbook and views a photo of a senior class 'Blues Brothers' party
Martin views a photo of sprinters racing toward a finish line in the yearbook
Martin examines Debi Newbery's senior portrait in the yearbook

name: Grocer Accepts Job and Receives Payment Confirmation
description: Grocer enters the main room of the villa-style A-frame and moves to an antique oak desk. He sits in front of a computer and clicks 'OK' on a prompt for remote access. On the screen, details appear: a request for availability in the Detroit area for two days, terms listing $560,000, and an option to confirm. He selects 'Now' and clicks 'OK / FAX materials.' Leaning back, he sips his juice. The fax machine on the desk rattles, and the computer emits a beep. A confirmation number for a wire transfer—AJ6687-OI99471—appears on the screen. Grocer presses the return button after noting the number. The screen changes to 'Connection is terminated / Status idle.' Moments later, the fax machine begins to moan and chatter. Grocer lifts his juice glass in a slow toast toward the computer.
related_events: Grocer accesses remote system for job assignment in Detroit
Wire transfer confirmation is received by Grocer

name: Grocer Confirms Transfer and Ends Connection
description: After reading the confirmation number on the screen, Grocer presses the return button. The computer displays a message: 'Connection is terminated / Status idle.' The fax machine begins to moan and chatter. Grocer leans back, raises his juice glass toward the computer in a slow, lazy toast.
related_events: Grocer terminates connection and returns system to idle state

name: Grocer Receives Documents by Fax
description: After confirming the job details and payment on the computer, the fax machine on the antique oak desk begins to rattle. It prints out the documents as the machine emits a low moaning and chattering sound. The grocer leans back in his chair, sips his juice, and raises the glass in a lazy toast toward the computer screen.
related_events: Fax machine receives documents following job confirmation

name: Grocer Toasts the Computer with Juice
description: After the fax machine moans and the computer displays a confirmation message, Grocer leans back in his chair, lifts his juice glass, and offers a lazy toast toward the computer.
related_events: Grocer toasts the computer with a glass of juice

name: Martin Rejects Extra Job and Fends Off Grocer's Offer
description: Martin rides down FDR Drive in a Lincoln Town Car, speaking on the phone with Marcella. He tells her that handling the cyclist was the only job he was paid for, and he refuses to take responsibility for anything beyond that. As he ends the call, Marcella says, "Wait. I have Mr. Grocer for you." Martin tells her to patch him through. Another Town Car appears in the next lane, driven by the Doorman, who is now revealed to be Grocer, also on the phone. Martin asks what Grocer wants. Grocer proposes forming a group for professionals like them to combine their efforts, suggesting it could be like a club where they work less and earn more. Martin declines. Grocer insists, describing it as a natural evolution of their work, reminding Martin they used to run jobs together when he was starting out. He says everyone is joining and invites Martin in on the ground floor. Martin mocks the idea, suggesting Grocer could be a father figure to him, but Grocer ignores the comment. Martin refuses again, calling the group a dirty little guild and telling Grocer not to bother him. Grocer warns him, "I'm gonna get you, kid." Martin hangs up and pulls away, driving off.
related_events: Martin argues with Marcella about job responsibilities

name: Martin Rejects Grocer's Offer on FDR Drive
description: Marcella connects Martin with Mr. Grocer over the phone. As they speak, Martin notices another Lincoln Town Car pull up beside him in the next lane. The Doorman is driving, holding a phone to his ear—Martin realizes it's Grocer. Grocer proposes forming a club for elite assassins, a way to work less and earn more. He invites Martin to join, suggesting they could make big money together, targeting important people. Martin mocks the idea, sarcastically calling Grocer a potential father figure. Unfazed, Grocer reminds Martin of their past, urging him to join what he claims is an inevitable evolution. Martin refuses, calling the club a dirty guild, and hangs up. He pulls away, leaving Grocer behind on the road.
related_events: Marcella connects Martin with Mr. Grocer
Martin observes Grocer in another Town Car on FDR Drive
Grocer proposes a professional club for assassins
Grocer attempts to recruit Martin into the assassin organization
Martin rejects Grocer's offer and ends the conversation

name: Martin Drives Away from Grocer's Offer
description: After hanging up the phone, Martin steers the Lincoln Town Car off FDR Drive and accelerates, pulling away from the other Town Car in the adjacent lane. The Doorman, now revealed as Grocer, remains behind, still holding his phone as Martin disappears into the distance.
related_events: Martin drives away after the phone call

name: Martin Sees Felix and the Silent Exchange on the Street
description: Martin leaves the station, shoulders slumped, moving slowly down the sidewalk. He looks up and sees Felix walking ahead—wearing Le Coq Sportif sweats, head down, eyes distant. Martin frowns, recognition flickering, something unpleasant surfacing. He watches Felix’s gaze shift across the street to a parked Country Squire, where Lardner and McCullers sit in the front seat. Felix’s eyes lock with theirs for a brief moment—no words, no gestures, just a stillness that passes between them. Martin sees it all. Then his attention snaps to a man approaching nearby—square-jawed, wearing dark sunglasses, hand moving toward his breast pocket. Martin tenses. The man pulls out a glasses case, removes his shades. It’s Paul Swiderski. He grins, holds out his hand. Martin doesn’t react. Paul lowers his hand slightly, still smiling. 'Marty! It’s me. Paul.' Martin blinks, then slowly recognizes him. They shake hands. Paul shrugs. 'Hey. Give me a break.'
related_events: Martin exits train station in defeated state
Martin recognizes Felix on the street
Felix observes Lardner and McCullers in Country Squire
Martin witnesses exchange of glances between Felix and Lardner and McCullers
Martin notices armed man approaching with hand in jacket

name: Martin and Paul Swiderski Reunite on the Street
description: Martin watches as a man in dark sunglasses approaches him, reaching into his jacket. The man pulls out a glasses case, removes his shades, and reveals himself as Paul Swiderski. Martin does not recognize him at first. Paul greets him with a grin, reminding him of their past. Martin finally remembers, and they shake hands.
related_events: Martin fails to initially recognize Paul Swiderski
Paul Swiderski removes dark sunglasses and reveals identity to Martin
Martin and Paul Swiderski finally shake hands after recognition

name: Bodyguard Reacts to Scream, Martin Arrives with Gun Drawn
description: A muffled scream echoes from inside the apartment. The bodyguard, seated outside the door, jumps to his feet, drawing his gun. Before he can act further, the exit door at the end of the hallway slams open. Martin steps through, weapon already aimed. The bodyguard turns, leveling his gun at Martin. Martin shouts, 'Freeze! Police!' The bodyguard hesitates. Martin fires two shots, striking the bodyguard in the head. The bodyguard collapses. Martin approaches, takes a retractable keychain from the bodyguard's belt, and uses it to unlock the apartment door. He lets the keys snap back into place, then drags the bodyguard's body inside.
related_events: Bodyguard hears muffled scream and draws weapon

name: Martin confronts and kills the bodyguard
description: Martin bursts through a hallway exit door, gun drawn, and confronts the bodyguard. He shouts, 'Freeze! Police!' The bodyguard hesitates, his weapon still raised. Martin fires two shots, striking the bodyguard in the head. The bodyguard collapses. Martin approaches, takes a retractable keychain from the bodyguard's belt, and uses it to unlock the apartment door. He retracts the keys back onto the belt and drags the bodyguard's body inside.
related_events: Martin confronts bodyguard in hallway
Martin shoots bodyguard twice

name: Martin Retrieves Keys and Drags Bodyguard into Apartment
description: After the bodyguard falls, Martin reaches for his belt, pulls free a retractable keychain, and unspools the ring of keys. He inserts one into the apartment door, unlocks it, and lets the keychain retract back to the bodyguard's belt. Then he grabs the bodyguard by the arms and pulls the body inside, closing the door behind him.
related_events: Martin retrieves keys from bodyguard's belt
Martin drags bodyguard's corpse into apartment

name: Driving Through Grosse Pointe
description: Martin and Paul drive through Grosse Pointe, Michigan, where wide streets are lined with towering oaks and grand homes set back on lush lawns. Paul smokes a joint as they cruise past their old haunts. He explains he needs to take some people through a final walk-through of a property, promising to be quick so they can spend time together. Martin looks out the window, quiet, taking in the familiar surroundings. Paul jokes that he thought Martin might have joined a cult, half-expecting him to return wearing a fennel wreath and paper pants, then offers him the joint. Martin declines with a grin, saying there was no money in it. Paul retorts that he did the same thing Martin did—he stopped standing on the sidelines and got into the working world, telling Martin to ease up on the judgment. Martin nods, saying it’s fair. After a pause, Paul says again how good it is to see him. Martin agrees, and the ease between them settles like dust after a long time apart.
related_events: Martin and Paul drive through Grosse Pointe
Paul smokes a joint during the drive
Paul explains his plan for a final walk-through
Martin reflects on the past while looking out the window

name: Jokes and Confessions in Grosse Pointe
description: Paul and Martin drive through Grosse Pointe, Michigan, past wide streets and grand homes shaded by oaks. Paul smokes a joint and offers it to Martin, who declines. Paul jokes that he expected Martin to return wearing a fennel wreath and paper pants, relieved he hadn’t joined a cult. Martin smirks and says there was no money in it. Paul asks what happened to him, and Martin turns the question back. Paul says he got off the sidelines and joined the working week, telling Martin to stop acting superior. Martin nods and says it’s fair. Paul repeats that it’s good to see him. Martin agrees, and a quiet moment settles between them.
related_events: Paul expresses relief at Martin's return
Martin questions Paul about the lack of money in the plan
Paul explains his decision to join the workforce
Martin acknowledges Paul's explanation

name: Paul and Martin Reconnect in Grosse Pointe
description: Paul looked at Martin and said again, 'Goddamn, it's great to see you.' Martin met his gaze and replied, 'You too.' The words hung between them, simple and unforced, as the quiet ease of their old friendship settled back into place.
related_events: Paul expresses renewed joy at seeing Martin
Martin reciprocates Paul's sentiment of camaraderie

name: Martin Prepares the Chalice in the Empty Church
description: In the darkened church, Martin approaches the altar and opens the gilded cabinet. He takes out the chalice, squirts a clear liquid into it, swishes it around, and then returns it to the cabinet. Later, during a crowded church service attended by Mann, the priest lifts the chalice, murmurs a prayer, and drinks from it before collapsing behind the altar. The chalice slips from his hand and rolls across the carpet. Martin sits in a back pew, watching silently.
related_events: Martin prepares the chalice with a clear liquid
Martin reflects on the church purging itself of its pedophile

name: Priest Collapses After Drinking from the Chalice
description: During the church service, the priest lifted the chalice, murmured a prayer, and took a drink. Moments later, he collapsed behind the altar. The chalice slipped from his hand, fell to the carpet, and bounced slightly before coming to rest.
related_events: Priest drinks from the chalice and collapses during service
Chalice falls from priest's hand and bounces on altar carpet

name: Martin's Voiceover and Dr. Oatman's Accusation
description: From the back of the darkened church, Martin mounts the altar and opens the gilded doors to reveal the chalice. He removes it, squirts a clear liquid into the cup, swishes it out, and returns it to the cabinet. His voiceover plays as he reflects on how the church seems to be purging itself of its pedophile. Later, he sits in a back pew of the now crowded church, watching silently as the priest lifts the chalice, murmurs a prayer, and drinks from it—then collapses behind the altar. A close-up shows the chalice bouncing free from the priest’s hand as it hits the ground. Martin’s voice continues, saying it’s a bull market, and adds that he was once the prodigy, but now he’s just one of the guys. Dr. Oatman’s voice is heard from off-screen, suggesting that the discomfort Martin feels might be guilt, remorse, over the innocent people he’s killed.
related_events: Martin expresses ironic reflection on his diminished status
Dr. Oatman suggests Martin is experiencing guilt and remorse

name: Dispute Over a Past Encounter
description: LARDNER and MCCULLERS sit at the edge of an airport bar, watching the crowd. MCCULLERS says he saw the man in Lisbon seventeen months ago while posting a walk, and adds that he believes he also spoke with him in Bonn. LARDNER interrupts, surprised the sighting was in Portugal, and counters that according to the file, the man hasn’t been in Portugal since 1990. As they talk, Martin passes by in the distance, moving down the hall. Without looking at him, LARDNER and MCCULLERS stand, drop cash on the bar, and head out, their conversation fading as they follow Martin into the terminal.
related_events: LARDNER and MCCULLERS observe the crowd at an airport bar
MCCULLERS recalls seeing a man during a walk in Lisbon seventeen months ago
LARDNER expresses surprise about the location of the Lisbon sighting
MCCULLERS claims he spoke with the target in Bonn
LARDNER challenges MCCULLERS's account based on file information

name: Lardner and McCullers Follow Martin Through the Terminal
description: Lardner and McCullers sit at the edge of the airport bar, watching the crowd. As Martin walks past them down the hall, they fall silent, stand abruptly, and drop cash on the bar. Without a word, they exit the bar and follow Martin through the terminal, moving with the flow of travelers until they blend into the crowd.
related_events: Martin walks past LARDNER and MCCULLERS in the airport terminal
LARDNER and MCCULLERS abruptly leave the airport bar
LARDNER and MCCULLERS follow Martin through the terminal

name: Lardner Mocks McCullers with a Solo Mission Suggestion
description: McCullers insists he saw the man in Lisbon and believes he even spoke with him in Bonn. name: Martin Discovers the Hidden Surveillance Device

A woman’s voice speaks through the headphones, addressing alumni and recalling old memories. His eyes open suddenly. He turns his head, cupping the headphones with his hands, sensing something off. He applies three drops of blue liquid onto the thread. The drops travel down the line, descending toward the sleeping man. On the monitor, the man’s face fills the screen as the fiber-optic follows the liquid. The man snorts, turns his head— one drop falls, landing on his cheek instead of his mouth. His eyes snap open, staring directly into the camera. Martin jerks the fiber-optic cable back up through the hole. 'Fuck!' he whispers. He quickly shoves all the equipment into an open duffel bag and leaves the room.
